name: chain
description: The chain module (shruggr/skein#78, #79): the one writer of the instance's chain state — headers, transactions, proofs, spends, settlement, broadcasts — under chain/state; everyone else reads it by CID. Box chain: the host's events (chain {root, height} from its headers tracker — the host chain's record, which the state points at, shruggr/skein#156 — and proof from its broadcaster: the `event` row, never a message), and {fn: ingest | status | proof, args} from the instance's own apps (the wallet, overlays: `$self`, by the host's loopback) and the owner; box chain/status (written status: a box is relative to the app, shruggr/skein#128): the status provider's messages (optional: left out on a host with none). Ingest a BEEF (shruggr/skein#121: the callers' rows name the filter beef, so the kernel's door hands ingest the pointer record's CID — the transactions and BUMPs blocks in the store, every BUMP checked against chain/state — never the bytes): proven, answered at once; unproven, recorded and broadcast. 0.8.0: every status of a transaction (accepted, mined with its height, rejected, reorged) is recorded and emitted as the fact chain/tx/<txid> {status, height?} — no watchers; listeners rest on the name. 0.9.0: a status is the latest fact — a valid proof makes a transaction mined also after a rejection (skein-sdk 0.18.0; the settlement record stays, read for its reason). 0.10.0 (David 2026-11-09): a status is one of four — pending (at intake, held and broadcast asked for, no answer yet), seen (was accepted; after a reorg with reason reorged), mined (height), rejected (reason; by: the winner of a double spend, or the root of an input-rejected cascade) — and EVERY transaction gets one at intake (mined when it comes proven, BEEF ancestors too); each output a transaction spends has a state, the fact chain/output/<txid>.<vout> {state: spent | rolledBack, spentBy}, its latest message its current state: when the app first holds a transaction it subscribes (on) to chain/tx/<txid>, and each of that transaction's status facts walks the outputs it spends from the chain state and posts what changed; ingest is also an in-VM call from a program's step (the app writes, subscribes, emits the statuses and the broadcast in that step; answered {txid, status, height?, reason?, by?}). 0.11.0 (David 2026-11-10): the linkage between a transaction and where its proof is is a fact — when a merkle path is saved, every transaction it covers (each level-0 hash whose root, computed through the path, is the header's on our best chain), held or not, is linked once and raised as chain/proof/<txid> {block, height, position}; a transaction taken in is subscribed to its own chain/proof (and read at intake: covered already, it is mined at once and never broadcast), and a later linkage wakes it: the step settles what the proof settles and raises chain/tx/<txid> mined. docs/CHAIN.md.
